title: Actual slice frames for norm-continuous internal modules
statement: For a scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme] and a normed field $A$, use the all-continuous ring and lisse modules of [def-sfb-norm-continuous-monodromy-data]. Let $R$ be its sectionwise ring sheaf under the recorded internal/section-module equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. For an internal module $M$, a pro-etale object $U$, and $n\geq0$, define a frame to be an isomorphism $R|_U^n\simeq M|_U$ on the slice [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Its $i$th column on any further slice object is the image of the $i$th standard generator, and scalar multiplication is the actual section-module action. For integral $X$ and a separable closure $k^s/k$ [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-pd-separable-closure], define restriction of a column to generic sections by the actual internal pullback unit evaluated on a lift $\operatorname{Spec}k^s\to U$ [def-sfb-normal-generic-lisse-sections]. Define the completed module by ordinary internal scalar extension [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] along the completion inclusion [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion]. Package the lifted group $\operatorname{GL}_n(\widehat A)$ with its usual topology and supplied open-subgroup-basis and two-sided-completeness proofs as a coefficient group. For a continuous right torsor [def-sfb-continuous-right-torsor], a frame presentation consists of bijections between its sections and these actual slice frames, commuting with every restriction and the right matrix precomposition action. Matrix coefficients are tested under the canonical continuous-ring comparison [def-sfb-continuous-ring-canonical-comparison]. For a normalized generic fibre functor [def-sfb-normal-generic-lisse-fiber], its matrix in a basis is the matrix of its Galois action. These definitions assert no existence of a frame torsor or basis.
